recipe_inventory.label: Kim et al. (2001): Upstream pristine bulk BTO preparation

source_locators.locator: Main PDF p. 1, Preparation and exfoliation paragraph

recipe_inventory.scope: Upstream bulk BTO support; missing firing duration precludes additional direct recipe credit.
gaps: Complete supplied three-page main and identity-matched eleven-page SI, including all figures, crystallographic tables and numbered references/experimental notes. Cited full sources unreviewed.
Absolute Bi2O3/TiO2 charges, firing duration/ramp/atmosphere and pellet pressure are unreported. This upstream bulk preparation remains supporting context.

Lithiation is described as 3-mol excess n-BuLi for at least three days: no absolute n-BuLi or BTO charge, hexane volume, solution concentration, reaction temperature or atmosphere is supplied. Vacuum-drying conditions are unknown.

Water addition volume, exfoliation contact time/temperature, wash volumes/count beyond several, ultrasonic frequency/power and suspension concentration are not supplied. The centrifugation speed is rpm, not relative centrifugal force.

The main text juxtaposes CTAB (~10^-3 M) / PAA (~2000 molecular weight, 0.1 wt%) with slash notation; whether these are alternatives or a combined formulation is unresolved. HRTEM preparation explicitly uses aqueous 0.1% PAA. No missing mixing ratio or combined-stock composition is invented.

PC and DMF are stated as EPD suspension media, but Figure S3 and its approximately 850 nm thickness are not assigned to one solvent. Electrode spacing, deposition area, suspension charge/concentration and solvent-exchange method are unreported.

All SI atomic positions, cell metrics and bond lengths refer to the bulk Li2Bi4Ti3O12 intermediate, not measured coordinates of the exfoliated nanoplatelets or deposited film. No CIF or finite-particle model is claimed in this delivery.
AFM profile/height values, HRTEM flake thickness and EPD film thickness are separate specimens/scales. Resin section thickness is an analytical cutting setting, not platelet thickness.

SI Figures S3a/b are nearly black in the supplied PDF render. Source captions/text support qualitative film description and approximate thickness; contours, porosity and new measurements cannot be recovered from these images.
No ferroelectric, dielectric, optical or electronic performance measurement is reported here. Application statements are cited background/outlook.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending.

source_notes.label: Intercalation and water exfoliation
source_notes.summary: The authors attribute blackening to partial Bi/Ti reduction during n-BuLi intercalation. Water removes lithium as LiOH with hydrogen evolution, separating the perovskite and Bi2O2 layers. The printed reaction is retained as an attributed mechanism, not a newly balanced or quantified gas reaction.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1, Preparation and exfoliation paragraph

source_notes.label: Separate structural scales
source_notes.summary: Neutron refinement gives the bulk LiBTO unit cell and atomic positions. AFM measures exfoliated platelets on silicon; HRTEM studies PAA/resin sections. EPD assembles platelets into a much thicker film. These objects and dimensions are not interchangeable.
source_locators: SI PDF p. 1–11, Crystallography and film data

source_notes.label: Film assembly
source_notes.summary: The source deposits BTO from PC or DMF under 12 V for one hour at room temperature without thermal treatment. Approximately 850 nm belongs to the illustrated as-deposited film, whose solvent is not identified. Dense/flat/oriented is the authors’ description; the supplied dark SEM images do not support new contour measurements.
source_locators: SI PDF p. 2–3, 6, 10–11, EPD and Figure S3

source_notes.label: Properties and outlook
source_notes.summary: Electrical insulation, ferroelectric memory, diffusion barriers and electron transfer are cited motivations. This paper supplies structural and compositional observations, not new quantitative functional-property tests.
